paths.description: Homepage/listing shell, primary browse entry, global navigation, preferences, performance, privacy and memory conditions.
Category-index archetype representing taxonomy discovery and a second long card-grid template.
Primary search-results journey using a non-sensitive generic query.
Sitemap-selected media-detail archetype representing title metadata, player affordance and related-content navigation; playback was not started.
Primary account form and blank-submission recovery state; no credentials were entered.
Unknown-route HTTP failure state and recovery path.

findings.summary: The site imposes one dark palette instead of following the user’s theme preference.
findings.evidence: Light and dark screenshots are pixel-identical; the platform probe reports colorScheme "normal", and static CSS contains no color-scheme or prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide light/dark tokens selected with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Motion is not adapted for reduced-motion users.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, computed transitions of 0.25s to 0.5s remain on menus, buttons and navigation; static CSS has no reduced-motion media query.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential transitions in a no-preference query and reduce or remove them under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: The UI does not adapt to increased contrast and already contains low-contrast text.
findings.evidence: The increased-contrast screenshot is unchanged, static CSS has no prefers-contrast/forced-colors rule, and axe reports 3.74:1 and 3.95:1 text contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations and raise text contrast to WCAG AA.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation changes abruptly.
findings.evidence: The site is an MPA and production CSS contains no view-transition-name or @view-transition rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for repeated shell and thumbnail-to-detail navigation, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long listings provide no scroll-state-aware navigation or progress affordance.
findings.evidence: Homepage and category pages are over 4,000 CSS pixels tall, while the probe finds no fixed/sticky chrome and CSS contains no scroll-state or scroll-timeline rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sticky, scroll-state-aware compact header or lightweight progress/return affordance.

findings.summary: Dropdown navigation is custom-positioned without anchor positioning.
findings.evidence: The DOM exposes custom .dropdown__content/.cat-drop menus; static CSS has no anchor-name or position-anchor usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with fallback positions for dropdowns near viewport edges.

findings.summary: Rich navigation uses ad-hoc dropdown containers rather than semantic platform primitives.
findings.evidence: The platform probe finds zero dialog, popover or details elements while custom dropdown containers are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover for transient menus, details for disclosures, and declarative light-dismiss where appropriate.

findings.summary: The desktop-width layout is forced into a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout metrics report scrollWidth 769px against a 360px visual viewport, a 409px overflow, on home, categories and detail pages; the mobile screenshot clips navigation, banner text and cards.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace fixed/minimum widths with intrinsic fluid layouts, wrap navigation, and test every template at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Repeated card and navigation components do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: The production CSS and live computed-style probe find no container query containers or @container rules; reused cards remain in a clipped desktop grid on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable grids/cards containment and adapt columns and controls with container queries.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is suppressed on key controls and several focusable links have zero-size hit areas.
findings.evidence: The focus probe reports outline none on the language button, search input and search button, plus repeated visible focusable anchors sized 0x0.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strong :focus-visible styles, remove empty focusable links, and preserve at least 44px touch targets for controls.

findings.summary: Error and recovery states are missing or unhelpful.
findings.evidence: Blank login submission leaves the page visually unchanged, and an unknown route returns a bare nginx 404 with no home, search or retry link.
findings.suggestedFix: Show inline, announced login errors and serve a branded 404 with search and safe navigation back to content.

findings.summary: Lab LCP is outside the good threshold under Lighthouse mobile conditions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports LCP 2.9s (performance 0.93), although the unthrottled trace reports 1.13s and CLS 0; the slower representative condition does not meet the 2.5s good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP image/content and trim early third-party work; verify field LCP and INP.

findings.summary: Synchronous first-party scripts and tracking chains add avoidable delivery cost.
findings.evidence: HAR identifies two parser-inserted classic scripts without async/defer; GTM is the slowest request at 1.3s and the network includes six redirects.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical first-party scripts, shorten tracking chains and preserve long-lived cache headers for versioned assets.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 240KiB unused JavaScript and 21KiB unused CSS; HAR attributes about 296KB to two GTM bundles alone.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate analytics loaders, split page-specific code, and load optional features only after intent.

findings.summary: Important controls and form fields lack accessible names or explicit labels.
findings.evidence: axe reports the search icon button has no discernible name; the login probe finds username/password controls without labels, and the image audit finds two missing alt attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an accessible name to icon buttons, explicit labels to login fields, and appropriate alt text or empty alt for decorative images.

findings.summary: Some secondary text fails WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: axe measures 3.74:1 for the age-verification subtext and 3.95:1 for “Top searches”, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use higher-contrast text tokens and re-test normal and high-contrast modes.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and focusable-element structure are unreliable.
findings.evidence: The focus probe finds key controls with outline none and 75 visible links without text, including multiple zero-size focus targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic controls with discernible content, remove empty anchors from the tab order and apply a consistent :focus-visible ring.

findings.summary: The experience fails narrow reflow and the custom media player exposes no caption track in the document.
findings.evidence: All three tested templates overflow by 409px at 360px. The detail probe finds no video/track element despite a visible player, so no caption equivalent is discoverable in the page DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix reflow at 320–400 CSS pixels and expose a semantic media element or equivalent caption/transcript controls.

findings.summary: Image delivery is dated and wasteful despite stable dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image audit finds 85/85 images in legacy formats, 64 without srcset and 30 rendered at less than half natural width; Lighthouse also reports 21KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP responsive sources with srcset/sizes and remove unused/repetitive CSS.

findings.summary: The login archetype has no document title or meta description.
findings.evidence: The login probe returns an empty document.title and the page is visually an unstyled isolated form, while home/detail metadata is descriptive.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every account page a unique title and concise meta description, or deliberately noindex private utility pages while retaining a meaningful title.

findings.summary: Video detail pages omit structured VideoObject metadata.
findings.evidence: The detail probe finds useful Open Graph video fields but zero JSON-LD blocks, so duration, thumbnail and content metadata are not exposed as schema.org VideoObject.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate VideoObject JSON-LD matching the visible title, description, thumbnail, duration and upload date.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but baseline security headers and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: Header inspection finds no CSP, HSTS or nosniff. Cookie inspection finds 11 cookies lacking Secure and PHPSESSID lacks HttpOnly while using SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS and nosniff; set session cookies Secure, HttpOnly and the narrowest workable SameSite value.

findings.summary: Multiple analytics systems track users immediately, before age verification interaction.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence identifies Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics and Yandex across six non-page origins; HAR records 54 cross-origin requests and 990KB cross-origin transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise to one necessary analytics path, defer it until a lawful user choice, shorten retention and proxy/batch events where appropriate.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only and lacks modern browser assistance.
findings.evidence: The login form exposes username/password controls with no autocomplete tokens; no WebAuthn/passkey surface is present. Permission states remain prompt, so no on-load browser permission prompt was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Add username/current-password autocomplete immediately and offer passkey registration and sign-in.

findings.summary: Most browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers include X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, but omit CSP/frame-ancestors, HSTS, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set CSP including frame-ancestors, HSTS, strict Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Navigation and content are cut off under a common viewport condition.
findings.evidence: At 360px, the custom desktop navigation extends beyond the viewport and the age banner text and card grid are clipped; the dropdown implementation has no anchor fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a true mobile navigation state and use resilient anchored/fallback positioning for menus.

findings.summary: The site declares standalone app display but is not installable/offline-capable as configured.
findings.evidence: The manifest has name/icons/display standalone but no start_url, and the service-worker probe finds zero registrations.
findings.suggestedFix: Either complete the PWA contract with start_url, installability fields and an offline fallback, or remove misleading app-like manifest intent.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling drops users into a server default with no recovery.
findings.evidence: A missing route renders only “404 Not Found nginx” and exposes no links, search, retry or route back.
findings.suggestedFix: Route 404/5xx responses through a lightweight branded recovery page with home and search actions.

findings.summary: Multilingual navigation exists, but the stylesheet is built entirely with physical direction properties.
findings.evidence: The home document correctly declares lang=en and Lighthouse validates hreflang, but static CSS contains 209 physical left/right declarations and zero logical-property declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain lang/hreflang and migrate layout spacing/positioning to inline/block logical properties; verify the German variant and RTL stress cases.

findings.summary: Privacy messaging is not matched by the page’s immediate tracking behaviour.
findings.evidence: The prominent age banner says “we don’t store personal data”, while before any age action the page sets 11 cookies, including 400-day analytics cookies, and loads Google/Yandex tracking.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate age-provider claims from site-wide privacy claims and obtain an honest, balanced choice before non-essential tracking.

findings.summary: The login form neither labels inputs nor explains invalid submission.
findings.evidence: Username/password inputs have no associated labels or required semantics; submitting both blank leaves the screenshot unchanged with no visible or announced error.
findings.suggestedFix: Add labels, required attributes, post-interaction validation, field-level messages and an aria-live error summary.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields opt out of browser autofill assistance by omission.
findings.evidence: The login probe reports empty autocomplete values for both username and password.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password, and preserve password-manager compatibility.

findings.summary: The account entry surface is visually broken and offers only password authentication.
findings.evidence: The login screenshot shows failed/absent site styling, extreme gaps and no surrounding navigation; the form lacks autocomplete and any passkey option.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore the shared account shell, make recovery/signup actions clear, add autofill and passkeys, and keep commitments/cancellation visible in downstream account flows.

findings.summary: Image assets are not delivered in efficient responsive formats.
findings.evidence: Image evidence finds 85 legacy-format images, 64 missing srcset and 30 oversized relative to display.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and use srcset/sizes so cards receive the smallest suitable image.

findings.summary: Background analytics work dominates script transfer without advancing the browsing task.
findings.evidence: GTM and Yandex account for roughly 386KB of script transfer; six tracking origins run during initial load before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate analytics loaders and defer/batch non-essential measurement until consent and idle time.

findings.summary: Third-party transfer is disproportionate on the media listing shell.
findings.evidence: HAR records 990KB of 1.07MB as cross-origin and 54 of 57 requests cross-origin; tracker evidence finds Google and Yandex systems active.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, consolidate analytics, self-host only justified assets and lazy-load media after user intent.

taskList.title: Fix responsive reflow across every template
Lock down headers, cookies and browser policies
Make login/account flows accessible, styled and recoverable
Respect color, motion and contrast preferences
